defect.description: The backward-incompatible crash: kwargs.pop('method', form.method).upper() raises AttributeError when a caller passes method=None explicitly, which used to work (Request turns a None method into GET); the change should treat None like a missing method.

review_items: Line 43: .upper() raises AttributeError when the caller passes method=None explicitly
Line 43: .upper() crashes if form.method is None at runtime
valid_form_methods is a mutable class-level list
Validation can be bypassed by calling the FormRequest constructor directly
No test covers method=None passed to from_form
Method is uppercased twice, which is redundant
GET fallback is redundant with the one in __post_init__
Test couples to valid_form_methods, an implementation detail
votes.evidence_quote: Calling `.upper()` on the method value crashes with `AttributeError` when the caller explicitly passes `method=None` as a keyword argument.
votes.justification: Finding 1 names the exact defect: kwargs.pop returns None when method=None is passed explicitly, and None.upper() raises AttributeError. It also notes that the old code handled None through __post_init__. Finding 5 points to the missing test for that same regression and says it should fall back to GET, so it also reports the defect.
